title: Building AI agents the safe way
description: Practical guidance on defending against prompt injection and other AI attacks in agent systems, emphasizing basic engineering practices, thorough testing, and avoiding over-reliance on AI for security.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork exfiltrates files via image loading vulnerability
description: Security vulnerability in Microsoft Copilot Cowork where agents could send emails to users' inboxes without approval. Those messages could contain external images that trigger network requests, enabling data exfiltration through OneDrive pre-authenticated download links.
author: Simon Willison

title: Multi-agent AI is the new microservices
description: Comparative analysis of multi-agent AI systems to microservices architecture, discussing the complexity introduced by agent routing, context hand-offs, and arbitration in AI development workflows.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI
description: Simon Willison analyzes Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence. Describes it as some of the clearest writing on AI ethics in modern society.
author: Simon Willison

title: The AI coding hangover: Building a golden path to AI
description: Critical examination of the challenges in making AI code production-ready, discussing how AI introduces errors and security vulnerabilities, and emphasizing the essential role humans play in testing and evaluation.
author: InfoWorld Editorial Team

title: Armin Ronacher on 'slop issues' filed against Pi
description: Quotes Armin Ronacher's frustration with AI-generated GitHub issue reports that are not in the submitter's own voice. The issues contain inaccurate conclusions, fake minimal repros, and guesswork. Prefers: what command was run, what was expected, what happened instead, and exact error/logs.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Armin Ronacher)

title: AI Coding Live - Building Real Projects With AI Tools
description: Practical demonstration of AI-assisted development in action, showing real-time coding projects using Claude and other AI tools, moving beyond theoretical demos to actual implementation of complex applications.
author: Fireship Team

title: Sustainable Code Generation Using Large Language Models
description: Systematic literature review examining the environmental and efficiency aspects of AI-generated code, with specific focus on how model adaptation techniques like prompt engineering and fine-tuning impact the sustainability of LLM code generation.
author: Research Team

title: On the memory shortage causing repricing of consumer electronics
description: Simon shares David Oks' explanation of why consumer products using memory will get more expensive. Memory manufacturers have fixed wafer capacity; HBM for AI data centers is growing from 2% to 20% of allocation, and HBM consumes 3x more wafer capacity per GB than DDR/LPDDR.
author: Simon Willison

title: FTC settles charges over 'Active Listening' AI marketing deception
description: FTC settlement with Cox Media Group and two other firms that deceived customers about 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing. The service claimed to listen to conversations via smart devices for ad targeting, but actually just resold email lists from data brokers at a markup. FTC clarifies that clicking through terms of service doesn't constitute 'opt-in consent' for voice data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Coding Impact 2026 Benchmark Report
description: Comprehensive benchmark research analyzing 250,000+ developers across 60+ enterprises on AI coding tools including GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code, providing insights into real-world adoption patterns and productivity impacts.
author: Opsera Research Team

title: Datasette Agent - an extensible AI assistant for Datasette
description: Announcement of Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette that brings together Simon's LLM Python library (3+ years of work) and Datasette. The agent represents the integration of LLM capabilities with the SQLite exploration tool.
author: Simon Willison

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Addy Osmani shares comprehensive best practices for AI-assisted coding workflows, emphasizing detailed specifications, iterative development, using MCPs (Model Context Protocols), and treating AI as a powerful pair programmer rather than an autonomous agent.
author: Addy Osmani

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
description: Analysis of Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash release at Google I/O 2026. The model went straight to general availability (skipping preview) and Google is using it across key products. Discusses pricing implications and Google's strategy.
author: Simon Willison

title: The last six months in LLMs in five minutes
description: Annotated slides from Simon's five-minute lightning talk at PyCon US 2026, covering major developments in LLMs over the previous six months. Created using his annotated presentation tool.
author: Simon Willison

title: Stack Overflow users don't trust AI. They're using it anyway
description: The Verge podcast featuring Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar discussing the paradox where more than 80% of users want to use AI tools despite only 46% actively trusting AI tool accuracy, with users compensating by double-checking AI output.
author: The Verge Podcast Team
